#2156. Manchester Re-United! Legends join forces to toast Sir Alex Ferguson on 40th anniversary of his appointment at Old Trafford

Published: 04:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 08:16 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his anniversary of being named manager of the club on Saturday night.

In a decision that ushered in the most successful period in United's history, Ferguson was poached from Scottish club Aberdeen 40 years ago on Friday – with the iconic manager lifting 37 pieces of silverware during his spell at Old Trafford.

He also played a significant role in shaping the careers of a litany of stars who graced the club during his 27-year tenure, with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and David Beckham hugely benefiting from his mentorship.

And a handful of players who shared a dressing room with Ferguson were on hand to toast the iconic manager during a celebratory evening in Manchester on Saturday night.

Diehard United fan and actor James Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside current United boss Michael Carrick.

Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea also joined their old mentor at the bash.

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez

Ferguson ushered in the most successful period in the club's history during his 27-year stint

Carrick has namechecked Ferguson as a crucial ally as he looks to transform United's fortunes amid the club's worst ever start to a Premier League season.

The Red Devils dropped into the relegation zone on Saturday night following Nottingham Forest's win over Manchester City, and Carrick's stint in the dugout appeared all but over following a 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

But he was handed a reprieve by the United hierarchy and there were green shoots of optimism following a rousing 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

United host Unai Emery's Aston Villa at Old Trafford today, and Carrick has admitted he has been given no guarantees on his future.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night,' he said.

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

What a fantastic evening at Old Trafford celebrating 40 years of Sir Alex taking the reign at @ManUtd. Catching up with the boys and some great speeches about how he achieved to leave such a mark on this club! pic.twitter.com/kgoNfzfPWJ

Ferguson unveiled as new manager of Manchester United in 1986

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

#2155. Man City star signs - What Charlton Athletic’s perfect January transfer window looks like

Charlton Athletic find themselves set for a hard-fought relegation battle down in the Championship and it could well be that good business done in the January transfer window is what saves them.

Having started the season with three successive victories and then a draw away at promotion challenging West Bromwich Albion at The Hawthorns, things looked as though they were on the up for Charlton.

Having survived the drop in their first season back in the second-tier last season, the expectation within the fanbase would have been to kick on this year and the start suggested that they will.

However, The Addicks then endured a ten-match winless run of form which only ended just before the international break with a 2-1 defeat of Sheffield United at The Valley.

Joint lowest scorers in the division, it is clear that Charlton need a spark in the final third and a general shift around in their squad and so we have taken a look at what would be an ideal winter window for the South Londoners.

A bit of a gamble but someone who could be a major surprise point of difference for Charlton in the second half of the season would be Younes Ibrahim, if they can get Brighton and Hove Albion to agree to loan out their starlet in the winter.

A mobile attacking midfielder will be a key addition for Charlton this winter with plenty of players having been tried but underwhelmed in that position – and Ibrahim, while very inexperienced, could be someone to provide a much-needed spark.

Bolton Wanderers and Derby County should prepare bids for former Charlton Athletic target Jesurun Rak-Sakyi this January

Brighton youngsters thriving in the EFL would not be a new thing and is perhaps a model for many to follow, with Amario Cozier-Duberry the best example on loan at Middlesbrough after his impressive stint with Bolton Wanderers last season.

The 18-year-old Egyptian is the latest prodigy coming through at the AMEX Stadium and an exciting first-team debut against Kauno Zalgiris in their UEFA Europa Conference League league phase opener, in which he earned an assist in a 4-0 victory over the Lithuanian champions, may well be a prompt for some EFL interest this winter.

A bit more known and recognisable to EFL followers and Charlton supporters but someone who is only who is even younger than Ibrahim at 17 would be winger Jeremy Monga.

Monga came through at Coventry City and then Leicester City before making his Premier League debut at the age of just 15 for The Foxes in the 2024-25 campaign before featuring on 27 occasions in the Championship last season.

He joined Manchester City over the summer before being loaned out to Swansea City but the sheer quality and depth of attacking talent that the promotion challenging Jacks have has limited Monga to being on the bench, and remaining an unused substitute, on just three occasions this season.

Monga is surely destined to have that loan stint cut-short but a Championship move still remains the likelier option for him and Charlton are crying out for some exciting wide talent and pace.

Moving away from the recruitment of young starlets to provide a spark in the final third, Charlton may well require a poacher in order to finish off whatever creativity is sought and produced.

As a result, they could do a lot worse than moving for Reading’s 32-year-old striker Jack Marriott, who hasn’t played Championship football since the 2021-22 campaign when he scored nine goals in 28 appearances for Peterborough United.

He has remained a consistent threat in the EFL, notching 16 in 24 League One games for The Royals last season before racing to nine across all competitions this season, albeit with injuries often disrupting him. With Jacob Brown and Jamie Reid now in Berkshire, though, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Reading deem a sale, for any fee but surely a relatively low one given his age, acceptable.

Matty Godden has had critics this season, albeit he did score their winner against The Blades at the weekend, and finding an upgrade on his profile; an experienced finisher for the level could well be a priority for Charlton.

Zach Mitchell came through the Charlton academy setup in 2022 but the 21-year-old defender has only gone on to make 20 appearances across all competitions for the club with loan spells at Colchester United, Saint Johnstone twice and Hibernian in recent seasons.

Still young, it could well be that Mitchell moves away from The Valley on a temporary basis initially but out of contract next summer and without a squad number this season, his departure feels fairly inevitable at this stage.

Another defender who could well depart this winter would be Kenya international Collins Sichenje, who signed for Charlton from Serbian outfit Vojvodina in February.

The 23-year-old managed just six appearances in the second half of last season with just three starts. This time around, he came off the bench to defend 2-1 victories against Derby County and West Ham United in August but hasn’t been seen since in the league, with a couple of other substitute appearances in the EFL Cup and his departure would also feel quite likely.

Following their promotion in 2025, Charlton brought in a fair few attackers that had previously thrived at a lower level and many have failed to make too much of an impact and one of them is Harvey Knibbs.

The former Cambridge United and Reading man struggled to find form and consistency in the conservative approach and setup of Jones last season and he managed just two starts thus far this season in defeats against Middlesbrough and Bolton Wanderers. To free up space in attack and also for himself to get game-time, a move this winter would surely suit all parties.

Birmingham City have won six of their last seven Championship games to surge to the top of the table after 15 matches. BCFC are in a fine position as the November international break continues, and the work of Chris Davies has drawn significant praise.

There have been doubts over his Blues future at times, especially during a disappointing 2025/26 season, but Davies has completed an impressive turnaround to secure his position. And, one man who believes the Welshman’s work should be rewarded with a new deal is Birmingham Live’s Alex Dicken.

When quizzed on Davies’ contract situation in a fan Q&A, Blues reporter Dicken wrote: “I think they should give it a few months to allow the relationship between John Murtough (Birmingham City’s new director of football) and Davies to develop – and get the transfer window done and dusted – but it’s definitely something that should be looked at before the end of the season.

Davies started strongly as he led a strong Birmingham City side to a rampant League One title win. That was expected though, so the boss and his side rose to the Championship with a point to prove.

#2152. Premier League legend David Silva, 40, makes emphatic return to football with man-of-the-match performance - three and a half years after retiring

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:23 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 10:15 EST, 8 November 2026

David Silva made his mark in his first game since coming out of retirement after scoring on debut in a man-of-the-match display for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin on Saturday.

Last month, the Manchester City icon revealed he was lacing his football boots in a professional sense again for the first time since 2023.

The 40-year-old started for Sha Tin and broke the deadlock against HK Rangers from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Silva stepped up and coolly passed the ball into the bottom left-hand corner - sending Hong Kong Rangers goalkeeper Ka-Yu Yip the wrong way.

The playmaker's goal sparked mass celebrations from his team-mates and the fans in the stands - with many taking their phones out of their pockets to record the moment.

However, Silva's debut didn't go as smoothly as planned as the visitors equalised in the 65th minute through Ibrahim Yakubu Nassam.

Some Spanish guy just scored a penalty for Sha Tin#DavidSilva #hkpl #hkfootball pic.twitter.com/JCbiYZEKE0

David Silva scored for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin with this penalty in their 1-1 draw on Saturday

The 40-year-old celebrates with his team-mates after scoring against Hong Kong Rangers

Silva was named man-of-the-match, in what his first competitve match in over three years

With 11 minutes remaining, Silva was then booked before he was substituted in the 84th minute with his side down to 10 men following Maxwell Ansah's 81st-minute red card for a second bookable offence.

Despite failing to take all three points, Silva did collect the man-of-the-match award after the full-time whistle.

Sha Tin currently sit 10th in the Hong Kong Premier League with five points from their opening seven matches. They sit one point and place above bottom-placed Eastern AA, who occupy the sole relegation spot, and 14 points adrift of table-toppers North District.

Silva called it a day on his playing career back in 2023 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament while playing for Real Sociedad.

He is most famed for spending ten years at Manchester City between 2010 and 2020, where he won 11 major honours; four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups. Much of that time period, though, is now under scrutiny.

He also has a statue outside the Etihad Stadium, and won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, as well as Euro 2008 and Euro 2012.

Upon joining Sha Tin, ex-Valencia midfielder Silva said in an Instagram video: 'I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong.'

Silva will hope to lead his side to victory when they take on Southern District in the Hong Kong League Cup Losers play-offs on Saturday.

QPR refined their squad with a handful of incomings and outgoings in the summer transfer window. It has yielded good results at Loftus Road, but some of those who headed out the exit door have not found the fortunes they would have hoped for.

Among those in that category is goalkeeper Joe Walsh. The 24-year-old saw a loan move away from West London sanctioned, with Pierce Charles becoming the new No. 1 while on loan from Manchester City and new signing Calum Ward locking down the spot as his backup.

Walsh was sent to League One with Wigan Athletic, but things have unravelled fairly quickly for him in the North West. And, having lost his starting berth, QPR should be recalling him when the winter transfer window comes around.

Then, just before the end of the transfer window, Joe Whitworth was signed from Crystal Palace. The 22-year-old has since locked down the place as Gary Caldwell‘s starting shot-stopper, leaving Walsh to watch on from the bench in every league match since.

It must be noted that Walsh’s numbers are from a smaller sample size, but he recorded a save rate of just 40% compared to Whitworth’s 69.8%, and the QPR loanee’s xG prevented sits at -2.03 compared to Whitworth’s impressive +4.45 (all stats via FotMob).

In truth, Whitworth’s importance in goal means it feels unlikely that Walsh will reclaim his place. He has started in the EFL Trophy games – all of which have ended in victory – but the Hoops man was on the bench for the FA Cup clash at Boreham Wood.

The purpose of Walsh’s loan move away from QPR was to find game time. However, evidence shows he is not finding the opportunities needed.

#2150. Bolton & Cardiff should pounce on Sunderland striker Timur Tutierov

The January transfer window is looming into view and clubs across the EFL will be seeking to strengthen their squads in order to secure their goals in the second half of the season.

Two teams that are expected to be active are Bolton Wanderers and Cardiff City, who should both be aiming to bring in Sunderland striker Timur Tutierov this winter.

Both Bolton and Cardiff gained promotion back to the second-tier last season and they have both been competitive in the Championship, heading into the November international break sitting 14th and 18th respectively.

Bolton missed the chance to close in on the top half as they succumbed to a 3-1 defeat away at Derby County last week, having been ahead at half-time, but they remain a respectable seven points clear of the bottom three and the relegation places after winning the League One play-offs in May.

As for Cardiff, The Bluebirds’ performances may well have supporters believing they could have a tilt at the top eight and the expanded play-off spots. Goal scoring issues may not be forefront of their mind right now after coming from 4-1 down to beat Burnley at the weekend, a few days after giving up a three-goal lead to draw with West Ham United.

Both have laid a foundation for themselves and adding some extra depth and quality this winter could be key to their end of season aspirations – and Tutierov may well be a promising market opportunity for either.

Ukraine U21 international Timur Tutierov joined Sunderland from Ukrainian Premier League outfit Kolos Kovalivka in the summer of 2023 and it is only now that the 21-year-old forward is beginning to get first-team football at the Stadium of Light.

Capable of playing out-wide, Tutierov, who spent the second half of last season on loan at Exeter City in League One, has been linked with a move to Blackburn Rovers, too, recently.

Tutierov has benefitted from Sunderland having a small squad and injuries to strikers Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor, as well as Regis Le Bris not yet trusting summer signing Juan Riquelme Angulo, has prompted a rapid promotion to the first-team picture for the Ukrainian on Wearside.

Tutierov has continued to feature for Sunderland’s U21 side, and he even got a goal and an assist against Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy earlier this season, while filling in for the likes of Isidor and Brobbey.

Tutierov made his first Sunderland start in the UEFA Europa League last month as The Black Cats defeated Portuguese second-tier outfit Torreense away from home before he scored his first European goal for the club in their next game, a 1-1 draw with Lech Poznan in Poland.

Domestically, Tutierov has made two Premier League appearances, including a start against AFC Bournemouth a few weeks ago, as well as having played in both of their EFL Cup games thus far; again scoring in a 3-2 victory over Brentford in the fourth round.

Sunderland supporters have questioned Le Bris’ decision-making at times this season and there are question marks over the viability of Tutierov’s long-term future in the first-team picture but the Ukrainian has certainly shown some signs of promise in terms of his finishing and his ability to be a nuisance for a struggling side.

However, as Brobbey returns to full fitness and Haiti international striker Isidor also makes his comeback, there is an expectation that Tutierov is pushed out on loan again this winter, especially if Sunderland again reinforce their squad up-front, and Championship clubs should be ready to take a punt.

For much of the summer, Bolton pursued former Milton Keynes Dons striker Max Dean and it looked as though The Trotters were about to get a deal over the line before the close of the summer transfer window.

However, Dean’s move eventually collapsed and Wanderers instead only brought in Ryan Hardie on loan from Wrexham and Theo Bair on loan from Auxerre as an out and out striker to support Sam Dalby up-front.

A look at the 25 biggest clubs in England according to AI chatbot ChatGPT.

Hardie has badly struggled in his brief cameos for The Whites, while Bair has shown flashes of quality but a general inconsistency as well as being almost too similar a profile to main man Dalby in attack.

Another striker is a must for Steven Schumacher this winter and a striker of a different profile, one in which they can be a threat with runs in behind and off the ball, would be key.

Given his ability to play out-wide and with a bit of speed, Tutierov would surely fit that bill and, as he continued to gain some much-needed high-level experience, Bolton may well be the beneficiaries of a breakthrough season for the former Kolos man.

Cardiff have a well set and impressive style of football implemented by coach Brian Barry-Murphy and their style of football has not been short of goals with nine scored in their last two games against teams playing in the Premier League last season.

A theme of Barry-Murphy’s reign has been a trust in the youth setup and few signings have been made in his three transfer windows in charge, albeit the sheer volume of academy graduates has meant they have not remained short up-front.

Versatility is another key with plenty of players having played in a variety of positions for the Northern Irishman and that extends to up-front with the versatile Callum Robinson adept at filling in for first-choice striker Yousef Salech - though he's been banished in recent weeks.

Salech hasn’t been at his most efficient best this season but he has remained a threat and goals have started to come for the Dane, who like Dalby, would remain the main man if Tutierov was to sign.

What is required, though, is that depth up-front with only three players scoring more than twice in the Championship so far this season for Cardiff – one being Salech, another being winger Ollie Tanner and the other the all-action attacker that is Jack Moylan.

In terms of another out and out striker, Cardiff don’t really possess one and, while Tutierov can play wide which would be another virtue in a Barry-Murphy side, adding extra depth to sustain themselves in the second-tier feels like a necessity.

#2148. Inside the insane trophy room of Chelsea legend Branislav Ivanovic: Framed pictures of his 42 goals, a ring from Didier Drogba... and an LED football pitch

Published: 04:50 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EST, 8 November 2026

Legendary Chelsea defender Branislav Ivanovic's insane private trophy room has gone viral after a fan posted a tour of the museum online.

The now 42-year-old made 377 appearances for the Blues during a nine-year stint at the club from 2008 to 2017.

He enjoyed a hugely successful time with the west London side, winning ten trophies and becoming one of the club's most decorated defenders.

As well as winning three Premier League titles he landed three FA Cups,  the League Cup, the Community Shield and the Europa League. He also has a Champions League winners' medal with the Blues, though the Serb did miss out on playing in the 2012 final after famously being told by Geoff Shreeves live on Sky Sports that he was suspended following their win over Barcelona in the semi-final.

Branislav Ivanovic won 10 trophies with Chelsea across nine years with the Blues

The Chelsea legend has built a private trophy room in his hometown of Sremska Mitrovica to rival any other

In a video posted to Instagram a fan from Ivanovic's hometown Sremska Mitrovica explained he was allowed access to the private showroom and documented the breadth of trophies, personal honours and shirts he has collected throughout his illustrious career.

Many of the souvenirs are from his time in Russia with Lokomotiv Moscow and Zenit St Petersburg, as well as those he got at Chelsea.

The private museum holds over hundreds of shirts alone and has an entire wall adorned with shirts just given to him and signed by someone he either played with or played against including the likes of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Neymar and Javier Zanetti.

Most Chelsea fans will remember Ivanovic's most crucial goals such as his winners in the Champions League round of 16 against Napoli and the 2013 Europa League final against Benfica.

And the Serbian appears to have made an effort to immortalise every single one of his club goals by framing and displaying a photo of all 42 from throughout his career.

Amongst other quirky designs, the room has a set of football leg stools for guests to sit on at the bar

Mourinho gets a mention having won the Premier League, Fa Cup and League cup with the Serbian in the 2014-15 season

There is also a replica of every trophy he has won in his career as well and a specialty ring he received as a gift from Didier Drogba after Chelsea's 2012 Champions League triumph.

Ivanovic didn't forget to add some style to the room by installing an LED football pitch to light the room and putting swanky football leg chairs at a fully stocked bar.

He even has a slide solely dedicated to displaying quotes from his former manager Jose Mourinho including the Special One's description of Ivanovic as 'The Perfect One'.

Since leaving Chelsea in 2017 the Serb moved back to Zenit St Petersburg before ending his career back in England with West Brom in 2021.

Divin Mubama has struggled to lead the line in his absence, while Lewis Dobbin has arguably been asked to perform a role that does not suit his skill-set, having been used as a focal-point number nine rather than a winger or support striker playing just off of a number nine.

That has at least allowed Edozie to feature more regularly out wide, but the overall balance remains questionable. Whether Southampton send Mubama back and sign a specialist striker or recruit another versatile forward, Larin and creative influences such as Leo Scienza and Finn Azaz need considerably more support.

Kuryu Matsuki is an excellent option for Eckert due to his versatility, but there needs to be a rebalancing of the attack soon, especially if they have serious ambitions of automatic promotion. At Larin's age, they cannot just rely on the Canadian to perform Saturday and Tuesday most weeks.

Edozie arrived at Southampton from Manchester City and showed considerable promise during his first Championship campaign under Russell Martin in 2023/24, registering six goals and three assists in 34 league and play-off appearances.

However, a subsequent loan at Anderlecht and injury problems stalled his progress. He is now beginning to feature more regularly under Eckert, even scoring recently for his first Saints goal since February 2024.

#2145. Steven Schumacher confirms Bolton Wanderers boost

Bolton Wanderers boss Steven Schumacher has no long-term concerns about club captain Eoin Toal and expects to see him back from his current setback around Christmas.

The 27-year-old Northern Ireland international is currently recovering from an ankle injury he picked up in a training session he picked up ahead of their 3-2 defeat against Bristol City in late October. He's missed the last three games.

Toal has had a history of ankle problems dating back to the 2023 EFL Trophy final. This is said to be an issue with the opposite ankle, but it adds to the narrative amongst some Bolton supporters that the centre-back can't stay fit for lengthy spells.

Since arriving at the Toughsheet Stadium in the summer of 2022, Toal has played 155 times for the Trotters, but only managed 22 league games in his first season and 19 in 2024/25. Despite a decent injury record in the past couple of years, though, this setback has raised some alarm bells, which Schumacher was quick to quieten.

Toal missed the majority of Steven Schumacher's first half-season at the club, after he arrived in late January 2025. In his first full campaign in charge, though, the 27-year-old was nearly ever-present.

The Northern Irishman missed the play-off final win over Stockport County with a hamstring injury, but before then, he made 39 league and play-off appearances, while also being left on the bench four times. Indeed, he missed only six games, including that Wembley final.

Then this season, when Toal wasn't playing, he was unused from the bench. This setback is his first this year, and his first lengthy one in terms of missing consecutive games since the 2024/25 campaign. Therefore, Schumacher isn't concerned about his long-term fitness.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

"I think he will be fine – I mean, last year he played virtually every game up until the play-off semi-final,” Schumacher said, per the Bolton News. "He was available for pretty much every week and had overcome the injuries he had the previous season when we first came in.

"He had been really stop-start that first season, but I think he did enough to show that his body is durable, and I think he has been excellent for us. Injuries can happen; that’s football, but no, I don’t have any long-term concerns with Toally."

The Bolton boss was quick to outline that his recent injuries haven't been a recurrence of one issue, and his current ankle problem is "innocuous."

"He’s had a calf issue, this one is a different ankle, the hamstring at Bradford. And this one was such an innocuous thing. He just stood on somebody's foot and rolled his ankle," he explained.

"So, it's not ideal for him. But I don't think it's going to be a major long-term thing either. We will get him back out there as quickly as possible, and he’ll be fine."

Toal is in the final year of his Bolton deal, which he signed back in 2024. Wanderers fans appreciate his contributions, but believe that the Northern Irishman's time at the Toughsheet could be coming to an end given his injury record.

When the extent of his injury was revealed earlier this month, one Bolton supporter wrote on X, "Toals career at boltons coming to an end i think." In the replies, another fan agreed, stating, "He is always injured."

Even in response to Schumacher's comments, someone was rather skeptical in the replies, assuming that the Bolton boss almost had to say that to "maintain some market value," and that he "always seems to be injured."

Ultimately, it's a perception that will follow Toal throughout the rest of his time at Bolton, even if this proves to be his only slightly major setback in the last two seasons.

Do you think the perception of Eoin Toal's injury record is unfair? Let us know in the comments.

And if his contract is up at the end of the season, a lot of Wanderers fans may be happy to shake hands, thank him for his five years of service and move on.

Steven Schumacher has plenty of backup in the central defensive area, with the likes of Chris Forino, Lewis Brunt, Ben Davies and Akin Famewo joining Toal as senior centre-back options.

Therefore, a setback to the captain shouldn't leave Bolton too short of defensive options, but there's an argument to be made that having the 27-year-old fit and healthy wouldn't go amiss.

FLW gets AI to rank the friendliest clubs in the second tier this season

The Trotters have struggled defensively this season. No side has allowed more expected goals, and only Derby County and Cardiff City have faced more shots on target.

In the seven games that Toal has started, they have kept two clean sheets. They've also conceded at least three to West Ham United, Norwich City and Middlesbrough, but they went on to do that in two of the three he's missed due to this ankle issue.

Having the leadership of the Northern Irish international may be what Bolton needs this year. Even if his injury record is perceived to be poor, he's still a helpful player to have amongst the squad.

#2144. To infinity and beyond! Another stunning Diego Gomez strike has Brighton up to SECOND and daring to dream... as Brentford's Igor Thiago is goaded into a red card

Published: 11:08 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 8 November 2026

Onwards and upwards go Brighton. Another victory to send them soaring into second place with only Arsenal above them.

It is a lofty perch for the Seagulls and one more admirable when considering the depths from which they have risen.

Homeless and penniless, on the brink of extinction at the end of the last century they are now daring to dream about the Champions League.

To infinity and beyond. Why not? Fabian Hurzeler’s team have already beaten Arsenal and Manchester City without conceding this season.

The only goals scored against them in the last six Premier League games came at Liverpool, where they lost 2-0 but were not outplayed.

City’s season is mired in uncertainty, awaiting sentence for financial breaches and the other half of the traditional Big Six are so erratic there will likely be scope for interlopers when the prized European tickets are handed out in May.

It is six months away but at this moment in time there are not four teams better than Fabian Hurzeler’s.

Brighton appear fully formed. Delightfully fluent in attack. Creative with zip and imagination and different ways to score goals.

There is a defined style of play. Solid at the back with enough sporting maturity to survive a test of needle, which this became against Brentford after the red card for Igor Thiago’s red card.

Diego Gomez celebrated another memorable strike at the Amex Stadium after his halfway-line stunner in the 5-0 win over Crystal Palace

The Bees already trailed to a screamer from the left boot of Diego Gomez and went further behind before half time when Pascal Gross converted a penalty awarded for a shirt pull by Keane Lewis-Potter on Luka Vuskovic.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 6; Costinha 6, Dunk 6, Vuskovic 6, Boscagli 7; Gross 8, Andres 6 (Wieffer 46, ); Gomez 7 (Yalcoue 90+3), Ayari 7 (Hinshelwood 78), De Cuyper 7 (Minteh 82); Kostoulas 6 (Rutter 82)

Subs not used: Steele, Hadjam, Kadioglu, Svoboda

Bookings: Andres, Boscagli, Wieffer, Dunk

Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher 6; Kayode 5, Ajer 6, Van den Berg 6 (Wilson 70), Lewis-Potter 5 (Diouf 59); Sangare 5 (Jensen 59), Janelt 5, Hickey 5 (Collins 46); Ouattara 4 (Yarmoliuk 46), Thiago 3, Schade 4

Subs not used: Valdimarsson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Gross, the 35-year-old midfielder schemer who walloped his penalty into the top corner in emphatic fashion, embodies the confidence pulsing through this team and his goal closed the contest.

The Bees assembled in the deep looking to minimise damage with an eye on a counterattack or a set piece and maybe hoping the officials would see fit to even it up at 10 against 10.

It didn’t happen. Instead, Brighton controlled the ball. They have had more than 75 per cent of possession across 90 minutes and spent the second half probing around the fringes of the Brentford penalty area.

They registered 20 shots in all but there would be no third goal. And nobody minded. They celebrated the victory and a return to the Amex Stadium after five away games in a row and more than 5,000 miles on the road.

Every substitution made by Hurzeler came as a reminder of their strength and quality.

Kaoru Mitoma, yet to feature this season, is expected back from injury soon after the international break.

The Conference League is not proving a distraction to a squad of such depth and Hurzeler gave fans his permission to dream.

'They should be always excited,' said the Brighton boss. 'That’s our job. They can dream. They can have high expectations, but these are things we can’t control. We played good game but always things we can do better.'

This was Brentford’s second defeat in this Premier League season and they had players sent off in both.

'In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation, antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way,' fumed boss Keith Andrews, referring to Yehor Yarmoliuk’s red card against Liverpool, when the Bees finished the game with nine men.

'We should do better, but the game is in a state now and a place I don’t particularly like. And we’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.'

Chema Andres fouled Thiago, fell to the ground and sprang up to confront the Brazilian, who tried to push him away but caught him with a forearm under the jaw.

Igor Thiago's yellow card was upgraded to red after a VAR intervention

Andres collapsed for a second time. When Michael Oliver gave them a yellow card each it seemed fair, but VAR Stuart Attwell sent the referee to the pitch-side screens for a review.

Oliver studied the slow-motion replays and upgraded it to a red card. Off went Thiago, smiling wryly and shaking his head, dismissed for standing his ground and being goaded into a reaction.

He will miss games against Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal.

Opinions of Oliver in the away end did not improve when he gave a penalty for a shirt pull by 5ft 7in Keane Lewis-Potter which somehow sent 6ft 4in Luka Vuskovic somersaulting to the turf.

Vuskovic is already a favourite at the Amex Stadium and it is easy to forget he is only 19. He dominates in the air and reads the game like a seasoned central defender.

And after ten games he is ten points better off than those he left behind at Tottenham.

The Croatia international cannot be looking forward to yet another encounter with England. The two nations meet at Wembley on Thursday. England have put 11 past them in two games this year.

#2143. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2142. Bristol City & West Ham ticketing twist has caused a huge backlash

West Ham have enforced a major ticketing decision involving away supporters ahead of next month's home clash against Bristol City - and it's causing quite the reaction online.

Following West Ham's unprecedented relegation from the Premier League back in May, the London Stadium represents the away day for away fans throughout the Championship.

Indeed, the second-tier has never seen a larger ground than the London Stadium's 60,000-capacity, and for virtually every fanbase, an away trip to this corner of East London is one of the most notable fixtures on the calendar all season.

Fans of Bristol City, however, have just received a fresh twist that will impact their fixture away to West Ham next month, with the decision stirring up mixed reaction among supporters online.

Bristol City fans will be ticking off a major Championship away day when they travel to West Ham on December 12, though trips to Middlesbrough, West Bromwich Albion and Derby County are all on the agenda before their journey down the M4 and into East London.

But it has come with a twist that will now see a reduced number of supporters in attendance within the London Stadium away end, with West Ham having reciprocated the Robins' travelling allocation.

A ticketing announcement from the West Country outfit has confirmed this, disclosing that tickets will be on sale to supporters from next Wednesday before revealing the allocation.

Now, the Robins have informed fans that they have received an allocation of just 2,110 tickets including rail seats and general seating. This, of course, is a fairly sizeable reduction on the Hammers' typical away allocation to travelling supporters of around 3,000, yet they've simply reciprocated what City have already done.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

The development comes following an announcement in September which revealed that Bristol City have opened the Atyeo Stand to home fans for high-profile fixtures against West Ham, Stoke and Severnside rivals Cardiff, thus reducing the number of tickes available to away supporters.

Therefore, West Ham have reacted by reducing their own allocation for the Robins faithful, and unsurprisingly, it's sparked something of a stir.

With every other Championship club to have travelled to West Ham so far this season having received a larger allocation, fans were quick to react following the Robins' announcement.

A lot of the reaction actually came from Hammers supporters, who wasted no time in lauding their club's reciprocal efforts.

This one fan, for example, applauded his side and urged them to do the same for every game against an opposing club that doesn't provide the same allocation.

Another, meanwhile, kept it direct and straight-to-the-point in response to a Bristol City punter who had questioned the allocation.

Indeed, this West Ham supporter believes the decision is evidence of the East Londoners actually getting something right, with many simply all-too-happy to see that their club has refused to simply roll over and give out the largest possible allocations while being restricted in some of their own travels on the road.

By contrast, Bristol City fans have naturally failed to share the same sentiment and believe that the Robins have been hard done by with this particular decision.

A Robins supporter here pulled no punches by describing it as an "absolute joke" - to which the Hammers' lot were, of course, swift in reminding of why the allocation has been shaved.

Emojis can sometimes tell the story, too, and in this case, they summed up exactly how another supporter of the Ashton Gate side is feeling right now.

However, another punter saw sense behind West Ham's decision and has backed the reciprocation.

There has been a split of opinion over West Ham's allocation for the travelling Bristol City contingent next month, even if many do believe that the Hammers are perfectly within their right to match the reduction.

However, there's absolutely no division when it comes to the prices that West Ham are charging for Robins fans who intend on making the trip to the London Stadium, which may just work out among their cheapest away days all season.

Adult tickets come cheaper than virtually anywhere else in the Championship at just £25, whereas 66+ and under-21 ones are even more affordable at a price of £12.

Under-18 tickets, meanwhile, will cost no more than £10, with these prices across the board paling in comparison to some other second-tier clubs.

West Ham and Bristol City fans, what do you make of this ticketing decision? Is it fair? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

All in all, then, Bristol City supporters perhaps can't complain much, and in terms of how much the fixture will cost to attend, there can be no faulting the Hammers.

That's why this fan, despite the noise, took time to praise the prices for City's trip to face Scott Parker's side away from home.

It's also no shock that one West Ham supporter - and many more silently, one can only imagine - hopes that Bristol City undertake some reciprocation of their own by charging the same prices when the promotion-chasers travel to Ashton Gate on New Year's Day.

#2141. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2140. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2139. West Ham Insider Reveals Recruitment Mess Behind Club’s Decline

West Ham United are still suffering because of years of bad recruitment, Claret & Hugh has been told by a Hammers insider today. The source, who did not wish to be named, described the situation as a mess and laid the blame for the club’s current predicament firmly and squarely at muddled, poor recruitment.

Speaking to Claret & Hugh, the source said:

“It’s all down to recruitment and it’s been bad, a real mess.”

“It’s a hodge podge with players being brought from everywhere by loads of different people. We’re years behind and needed a complete reset, we had to start again and consider how we recruit.”

Honest words, and not ones that many West Ham fans would disagree with. The club has spent years changing managers, recruitment chiefs and transfer strategies, seemingly without allowing any one approach enough time to work. The result is a squad assembled under several different regimes, with little evidence of a consistent long-term plan.

It has always been Daniel Křetínský’s wish at West Ham to have a director of football in charge, and whilst we don’t have that exact job title at the club currently, Nils Koppen, as Director of Player Recruitment, is as good as a director of football in all but name.

What is clear is that the club are going to have to rebuild the recruitment structure brick by brick. And it’s worth pointing out that even as recently as the summer, there was still something of a mix-up, with a blend of recruitment ideas and Nuno Espírito Santo being allowed to bring in three players in Joël Piroe, Manor Solomon and Morato.

Kretinsky is a big believer in the structured recruitment model

That is hardly the definition of a joined-up recruitment strategy, although it’s also important to recognise that Koppen arrived with very little time to prepare for the summer window. The bigger issue is whether West Ham are finally prepared to commit to a consistent approach rather than changing direction whenever the manager changes.

We’re semi-lucky in one respect because we do have another transfer window coming up in January, giving Koppen and Scott Parker an opportunity to address some of the more obvious problems within the squad.

But this is definitely a time when West Ham have to commit to a transfer policy and allow it to play out and bear fruit over a number of seasons. Toying with an approach and then giving up, as we did with both Tim Steidten and Kyle Macaulay, is precisely the sort of short-term thinking that has contributed to the problem.

The club cannot keep appointing recruitment specialists, allowing them to start rebuilding the squad and then abandoning the entire project when results turn sour. At some point, West Ham have to decide what sort of players they want, how they’re going to identify them and who is ultimately responsible for bringing them in.

January offers an opportunity to begin correcting some of the mistakes, but the problems described by our source won’t be fixed in a single transfer window. If West Ham are genuinely years behind in their recruitment, the rebuild needs to be given the time and consistency that previous attempts have lacked.

I think the main problem has been David Sullivan’s autocratic dominance and net work of his agents. Let us hope we are now free of this and have a balanced outlook

Where’s all this money coming from to fund the (start of) this overhaul. I can’t recall all the figures now but debt in excess of £200m, some of which had to (and has been) repaid, losing £100m a year and whilst wages have reduced by, say 50%, so has revenue. Unless Kretinsky is now a 45% and the major shareholder ( there appears to be conflicting info as to whether this transaction has completed) he is, based on history, little chance of him providing a transfer kitty and even if he is how does ‘FFP’ come into the equation?

I don’t think we needed a club insider to tell us about this issue. Yes not all signings will work out, but our success rate has been particularly poor in the last 3 years. I am not against a manager making suggestions as you allude to with Nuno, but they must be agreed by all relevant parties, then it becomes a cooperative relationship between manager and DOF.

The issue is that poor recruitment rarely costs directly on the books. Players amortise and those that don’t work out at all go out on loan bringing in loan fees.

The real problem lies in the contributions that they do not make. We invest and don’t lose out on the books but we do lose out in having invested in a player who did not contribute for us.

That affects results so affects success so affects us financially in that respect. Repeated poor investments.

It seems a shame that Daniel Kretinsky was not exerting influence at the time when David Moyes was also trying to build a consistent team.

We had it all then. We needed to continue with the Jarrod Bowen type of recruitment. We needed to back the manager and his coaching staff.

Instead, we were treated to exotic ideas of radical change which turned out to be a waste of money, time and a football club.

Tim Steidten could not believe his luck and bank balance as he scoured the world for excuses to spend on as high a profile as possible players to add to and become the basis of his team. No thoughts as to how these players would work in the game plans with the other players we already had. Only a passing reference to the team coach as the stars were aligned. The manager’s fault when success on the field was not forthcoming.

Poor recruitment played its part but continuity and investment in building upon a solid foundation was the real problem.

Let us hope that Scott Parker is allowed to continue to build our new team and not just until a more exotic name like Pellegrini or Lopetegui gets whispered into the ears of Daniel Kretinsky.

We have an opportunity now. We must take it.

#2138. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2137. Billy Sharp sends EFL Championship promotion warning to Birmingham City

EFL legend and all-time Championship top scorer Billy Sharp has warned Birmingham City that there's still "a long way to go" after Chris Davies' side reached the second-tier summit ahead of the ongoing international break.

The Blues enjoyed an exceptional run of games between the three-week break in September and October and this current one, winning six of their seven games, three by at least a three-goal margin.

They dropped points only at Cardiff City, a side that has yet to lose at home this season, and have maintained their own unbeaten home record, winning all four games to add some gloss to a St Andrew's record which was pretty draw-heavy in the infancy of the campaign.

The win against former table-toppers Swansea City saw them climb above Middlesbrough on goal difference, and they will hold that top spot for at least another week until action resumes ahead of the Christmas period.

The question in the meantime, though, is: Can they stay there?

Billy Sharp has been a regular pundit on EFL shows this season, after formally announcing his retirement from the professional game back in October. The 40-year-old was promoted out of the Championship three times in his career, so he knows what it takes to maintain top-two form.

The all-time Championship top scorer waxed lyrical over Birmingham through the opening 15 games of the campaign, and was actually surprised that their run to the top of the table hasn't been given as much attention as it arguably should have.

FLW looks at which of the division's 24 clubs are the biggest and lowest spenders

"I think you saw glimpses last season, but they obviously didn't have that consistency," he told the Essential EFL Podcast. "They've done it really quietly, actually; no one's really spoken about them.

"He’s got the two settled centre-halves, which I've liked since last season, and I think he's playing a 4-2-3-1, which really suits him at the minute.

"He seems to have a settled side and had a little sprinkle with Millar coming in, adding a bit of magic down the left, and Stansfield got the two goals, which should do him a world of good. We know he’s got the ability, and when he’s firing, he can win games for Birmingham."

It's so far, so good for the Blues this season, but we are just 15 games in. With over two-thirds of the year still to go, and just one point separating Chris Davies' side from West Brom in fifth, Sharp feels that they can't rest on their laurels at all.

"Am I surprised they're top? I am," he admitted. "But we were saying this about Swansea on the last international break.

"It’s still tight at the top, fair play to Birmingham; going into this international break they are top, but there’s still a long way to go."

As Sharp mentioned, Birmingham's current run of six wins in seven to reach the top of the Championship has gone slightly under the radar, with the main second-tier narratives surrounding West Ham United's drop-off, or Middlesbrough struggling without Will Lankshear, for example.

Now, though, this Blues side are at the forefront of the conversation, and will be until league action resumes after the international break. Chris Davies' side are there to be shot at, and all eyes will be on whether they can handle the weight of expectation.

It's arguable that they didn't last season, with many expecting them to follow in the footsteps of Ipswich Town and make it back-to-back promotions after their record-breaking 111-point campaign in League One the year prior.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

But this year, the squad is much more settled. Partnerships which were forming last year are fixed now, and there hasn't been as much squad churn as there was last summer at St Andrew's.

Plus, Chris Davies' decision to move away from a patient, heavy possession-based style has worked wonders, with the Blues packing a real punch in an attacking sense due to their desire to get the ball forward quicker.

They look a lot more ready to maintain results and handle pressure as they become the side teams want to knock off the pedestal.

Sharp also spoke about how this exact conversation was being made around Swansea's chances at promotion, with Vitor Matos' side sitting atop the Championship at the last international break.

And while the Swans did return to action with back-to-back wins, they followed that up with four defeats in five leading up to the break, including that loss at St Andrew's last time out.

They're still in contention, sitting three points off Birmingham, but the difference in performances with the pressure on, compared to when it's not, was there to be seen, and Blues have to guard against the same happening to them.

Do you think Birmingham City can maintain this promotion-winning form? Let us know in the comments.

Chris Davies' side have a tough matchup at Stoke City when play resumes, which then leads them into a run of four games against sides sitting between 18th and 22nd. A win at the bet365 Stadium would propel them into a run of, on paper, easier matches.

Perhaps, by mid-December, this could be a side with some daylight between themselves and the chasing pack, and then people may be taking their current title charge a lot more seriously.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2134. Marco Rose's Bournemouth should not have the depth to win this many games domestically and abroad but at Ipswich they showed they can do it the hard way, writes JAMES SHARPE

Published: 11:20 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 8 November 2026

Juggling domestic duties with European adventures should not be as manageable as this for teams like Bournemouth.

Clubs of their size should be creaking under the weight of the extra fixtures. All those games, all that travelling. They have played nine games in a month.

Far bigger outfits have toiled spinning those plates. Remember when Ange Postecoglou stopped bothering about the Premier League entirely just to focus on the Europa League.

And yet here are those brilliant Cherries, three days after a win in Prague in that same competition, making it eight on the bounce with a victory at Ipswich thanks to Evanilson's opener, following goalkeeper Christian Walton's early howler, and an own goal from Leif Davis.

Bournemouth haven't done that since 2013 when they were getting out of League One.

Now, they are seventh in the Premier League, second in the Europa League.

Leif Davies reacts after scoring an own goal to make it 2-0 to Bournemouth

And they're in the League Cup quarter-finals – all while having the squad depth to name Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi on the bench.

Marco Rose's side showed they can also do it the hard way, too, after Jack Clarke's second-half penalty for Ipswich, given for a soft foul on Abdoul Ouattara, provided a far more tense final 15 minutes than anticipated inside a feverish Portman Road where Julio Enciso also twice went close from late free-kicks.

'One goal changed the momentum of the game and that's why I'm much more pleased about the last 20 minutes because we suffered but we did it together,' said Rose.

First James Trafford, now Walton. Bournemouth's win over Leeds last weekend also hinged on a goalkeeping howler, when Trafford's simple pass out from the back was intercepted.

This time Ipswich stalwart Walton took a back pass from Dara O'Shea and decided the best course of action was to try to dummy and turn Evanilson. He failed, of course.

Evanilson rolled the ball into an empty net. That intense Bournemouth press really can do some crazy things to you.

IPSWICH (4-2-3-1): Walton 4; Ouattara 5, Diop 6, O'Shea 6, Davis 5; Florentino 7 (Akpom 85), Palacios 6; Maeda 6 (Fatawu 65, 7), Enciso 7; Philogene 6 (Clarke 54, 7); Emersonn 5 (Flemming 54, 6)

BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 6; Smith 6 (Diakite 79), Hill 7, Silva 7; Truffert 7; Adams 7, Christie 6 (Cook 67, 5); Rayan 6 (Adli 86), Kluivert 6 (Kroupi 68, 6), Tavernier 7; EVANILSON 8 (Rodriguez 85)

After scoring the opener in Bournemouth's win last weekend, manager Marco Rose told Evanilson that he was becoming a 'real No9'.

That's six goals now in his last seven games but it's his all-round play that's so impressive.

He dropped in and played a beautiful curling through ball into the channel to set Justin Kluivert free down the right.

He collected the loose ball for the second goal.

He made a fine run to latch on to a free-kick over the defence to stab the ball over to James Hill at the back post, who headed over from close range, which would have put him level with Declan Rice as the leading assister in the league too.

'He's so hard-working,' added Rose. 'He does everything out of possession.

'He starts the press, he plays in between the lines, he gives us deep runs.

'But the most important thing is scoring and he understood that he also needs to arrive close to goal if he wants to score.'

If the Tractor Boys are to make their stay in the Premier League a longer one than last time, they cannot afford to keep giving early leads. The mountain is steep enough.

Evanilson's opener was the sixth time Ipswich have conceded inside the first 15 minutes of a league game this season. They are yet to score one that early.

A howler from Ipswich keeper Christian Walton gifted Evanilson the opener

James Hill celebrates Bournemouth's win which lifts them to seventh

It is what will make this defeat especially frustrating for Gary O'Neil against his former club. 'Gary, what's the score?' chimed the travelling fans.

For so much of the contest, Ipswich looked composed and confident on the ball, played with energy and intent and, after they pulled one back, showed how much pressure they can put teams under and how much this place can bounce.

They are a much better side than the one that came up last time but you cannot come out after the break and have Ouattara give the ball straight to Evanilson again inside 30 seconds as he did before Ryan Christie's shot took two deflections and went in.

'Gutted,' said O'Neil. 'To lose a game that you haven't been outclassed is tough to take. We restricted Bournemouth to nothing of their own doing. If you give the ball to the opposition number nine twice, it's going to be difficult.'

#2132. West Ham Linked With Argentine Goalkeeper As Parker Plans January

West Ham United have been linked with a move for River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán, with Argentine publication TyC Sports reporting that the Hammers are among the clubs monitoring the youngster. Atlético Madrid are also named as interested parties, although there is no suggestion that West Ham have made an offer or opened negotiations.

River Plate are reportedly prepared to discuss a departure if an offer of US$15 million or more arrives, with the club already considering how they might replace their highly-rated goalkeeper. Beltrán has enjoyed an impressive breakthrough season, making 45 appearances and keeping 19 clean sheets, while also earning recognition from the Argentina national team.

The reported interest comes at an interesting time for West Ham, with Scott Parker facing an increasingly obvious problem between the posts. However, I would suggest the goalkeeper situation is only one of two major priorities for Nils Koppen when the January transfer window opens.

West Ham sold more than £200 million worth of players during the summer transfer window and spent just under £40 million on recruitment. Therefore, I would already hope that there is money set aside for January, rather than it becoming a straight choice between signing a goalkeeper or a striker.

Koppen wants to sign a goalkeeper in January

The problems in front of goal have been well documented, with Koppen already making enquiries about potential replacements for Taty Castellanos. But the goalkeeping situation is arguably just as concerning, as the numbers surrounding Mads Hermansen make increasingly uncomfortable reading.

Parker cannot realistically expect to mount a successful promotion challenge if he doesn’t have confidence in his goalkeeper and continues to struggle to find a reliable source of goals.

As for the reported US$15 million valuation of Beltrán, I’m not going to sit here and pretend I’ve watched the goalkeeper play. I haven’t, and I’m certainly not going to offer a technical assessment of somebody I haven’t properly studied.

But if he is the right man for the job, realistically West Ham cannot afford to hesitate over paying that sort of money.

The club has already spent far too long muddling its recruitment strategy, and the appointment of Koppen should mean we finally have somebody identifying players who fit a longer-term plan. The recent focus on recruiting a new centre-forward is encouraging, but that cannot be allowed to become an excuse for ignoring the goalkeeping department.

I would like to think that the money generated by last summer’s sales gives West Ham sufficient financial flexibility to address both positions. This isn’t an either/or situation.

If Beltrán is genuinely the goalkeeper Koppen and Parker believe can improve West Ham, then make the investment. But don’t forget the striker, because we have problems at both ends of the pitch and neither is going to disappear by itself.
