#2131. Bradford City TV decision announced and it's causing a reaction

Bradford City fans have been left extremely frustrated by a television broadcast decision impacting their FA Cup tie against non-league Wimborne Town next month.

The Bantams have endured a dramatic opening to the new League One season, with Michael Duff recently replacing Graham Alexander as the man in the Valley Parade hotseat.

Duff has only overseen one league victory in West Yorkshire so far, but his new employers are certainly going well in cup competitions, yet to lose in the EFL Trophy whilst also making the EFL Cup quarter-finals and reaching the FA Cup second round.

Bradford comfortably dispatched Marine 7-0 on Saturday afternoon, with said victory being rewarded with a high-profile tie against Wimborne, the lowest-ranked side now left in the competition, after the Dorset club defeated League Two side Crawley Town 2-0 on Sunday.

There are, of course, plenty of former Premier League sides competing in the FA Cup's early rounds, and the likelihood of them competing against non-league sides increases the chances of television coverage.

Eight ties were selected for broadcast in the first round proper, and the same number have been chosen again for the second round between December 4th and 7th.

All 24 League One clubs have been ranked in order of size.

Bradford are one of six League One sides who will see their ties televised, with their trip to the Wyatt Homes Stadium kicking off the weekend on Friday, December 4th, with coverage beginning on TNT Sports 1 at 7PM ahead of a 7:30PM kick-off.

Other televised ties include 2021 FA Cup winners, Leicester City's trip to Dover Athletic, which now kicks off at 5:15PM on Saturday, December 5th on BBC Two.

It is approximately five hours' worth of travel from the West Yorkshire city to the town of Wimborne Minster, meaning that, at the best of times, an arduous journey would be in store for the Bradford fans.

Crawley supporters received an allocation of 500 tickets in the 3,250-capacity ground last weekend, and a similar number will be expected to make the trip to support Duff's men.

However, whilst City fans are likely to sell out such a figure, the decision to now play the game on a Friday night just three weeks before Christmas hasn't gone down well at all, with one supporter saying: "Asking people to take a day off work to go do a 10 hour round trip to Winbourne is crazy. Deserves boosted loyalty points imo."

Another said of the decision: "Friday night on the south coast. Seeing as there will only be about 200 tickets it should reduce demand."

"Did we really expect anything else - well actually the way the schedulers don't give a damn about travel times I had a feeling it might have been Monday!," one displeased City fan wrote.

"Who makes these decisions," questioned another Bantams supporter.

Bradford fans, will you be making the long journey to Wimborne for this FA Cup tie? Comment below!

Another verdict read: "Teed up perfectly for #bcafc to be on the receiving end of an FA Cup shock. Friday night, tight ground, locals right up for it, live tv....all the ingredients right there!"

"Honestly mind boggling who makes these decisions. Fair play to anyone who makes that journey on a Friday night," backed up the general feeling amongst Bradford's fanbase.

Wimborne are currently ninth in the Southern Football League Premier Division South, with four steps in the English pyramid separating themselves from Bradford.

As such, the wider public will certainly be hoping the non-league side reach the third round and potentially pluck out a 'glamour tie' involving a Premier League or high-flying Championship outfit.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Bradford, therefore, will be hoping they are not on the wrong side of a 'cupset' this time around, having been famed for such exploits in recent years during their run to the 2013 EFL Cup final and the 2014/15 FA Cup quarter-finals, where they came back from two goals down to defeat Premier League champions, Chelsea, at Stamford Bridge.

#2130. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

#2129. Scott Parker’s West Ham Training Plans Hit By International Call-Ups

Much has been made of the two-week international break giving Scott Parker his first proper opportunity to work with his West Ham players. Having taken charge just before the Cardiff City match, the new Hammers manager has barely had time to get his feet under the table, let alone implement his preferred tactics.

However, the truth is that Parker’s supposed two-week opportunity on the training pitch is nowhere near as useful as it sounds. West Ham have had ten first-team squad members called up for international duty, leaving the manager without several players who would ordinarily be involved in his starting XI.

Mads Hermansen, Tomáš Souček, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Manor Solomon, Joël Piroe and Mohamadou Kanté have all been selected for senior international duty. Edvin Austbø, Divine Mukasa, Airidas Golambeckis and Finlay Herrick were also named in age-group squads, although Herrick has subsequently withdrawn from England’s Under-20 squad, with the FA citing ‘injury’ as the reason.

That leaves Parker with a rather makeshift group of players to work with, although it should at least provide opportunities for others to press their claims for a starting place.

Assuming everybody is fit and available, the following is a possible starting eleven Parker could assemble on the training ground during the international break.

It’s not a bad group of players by any means, and the likes of Lewis Orford and Josh Ajala should welcome the chance to impress their new manager. However, it’s a long way from the team Parker is likely to select when West Ham face Preston North End.

Even something as straightforward as drilling the defence is going to be difficult. Whilst Morato can slot into a makeshift back four alongside Kilman, the likelihood is that Mavropanos will be Parker’s preferred centre-back when everybody is available.

And even if Mavropanos were to suffer an injury, I’d expect Golambeckis to be considered ahead of Morato. Unfortunately, both players are away representing their countries, meaning Parker cannot even work with what I suspect will be his first-choice defensive partnership or its most likely alternative.

It’s a similar story further forward, where Mukasa, Kanté, Austbø and Piroe are all missing. These are players Parker will need to assess and integrate into his preferred system, yet he’ll have precious little opportunity to do so before the Preston match.

Of course, there are positives. Parker can still work on his overall shape, passing patterns and defensive organisation, whilst giving some of the younger players an opportunity to impress.

But the idea that West Ham’s new manager has been handed two uninterrupted weeks to transform his team is somewhat misleading. He has time on the training pitch, certainly, but not with many of the players he’ll actually need when the Championship resumes.

#2128. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

Lisandro Martinez could return to Manchester United’s starting line-up against Leeds United this weekend, with the defender reportedly available for selection after the controversy surrounding his comments about the club’s summer transfer business.

TEAMtalk transfer insider Graeme Bailey has suggested Michael Carrick could bring the Argentine straight back into the team for the trip to Elland Road. The fixture is expected to be a hostile occasion, making Martinez’s potential involvement an interesting one.

#2126. Liverpool played like a team fighting for their manager, but Pierre Sage looks like a dead man walking, writes LEWIS STEELE - as Reds clinch morale-boosting win at sorry Crystal Palace

Published: 11:14 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 13:00 EST, 8 November 2026

By this time of the season, spirited performances mean little if you don't have the results to go with it.

Pierre Sage, who was sacked at Lyon two years ago, knows as much as anyone that this is a results-based business.

And he simply has not had enough results. Despite having Liverpool on the ropes at times here, Crystal Palace failed to land a knockout blow and that could be that for their under-fire manager, who looked like a dead man walking when he trudged off the pitch at full-time with a face like thunder.

Former Lens over-achiever Sage now seems set for a stuffing six weeks before Christmas and though he may curse at the small margins that denied his team a chance of a heavyweight and potential job-saving scalp here, the boss knows two wins in 10 league games is not good enough.

Liverpool, meanwhile, had the width of the crossbar and a throwback performance from goalkeeper Alisson to thank. In contrast to Sage, Andoni Iraola's side showed grit and determination to win when far from their best.

Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak all scored as the Reds put a tough week behind them that saw them lose back-to-back games for the first time in the Iraola era, which prompted a chorus of the old terrace classic 'Poetry in Motion'.

Florian Wirtz scored a rare Liverpool as they won 3-1 at Crystal Palace in the Premier League

Wirtz scored Liverpool's second on 54 minutes as they ran out as 3-1 winners at Selhurst Park

Things are looking ominous for under-pressure Palace manager Pierre Sage after another loss

This performance was hardly William Wordsworth levels of poetry and Liverpool were far from on song during large swathes of this match but when it really mattered, the attackers demonstrated just why the club spent so much money on them.

CRYSTAL PALACE (3-4-2-1): Henderson 5; Lerma 6, Richards 6, Disasi 5; Mingueza 6 (Khalali 87), Wharton 5, Timber 6 (Timber 60, 6), Mitchell 6; Kamada 6, Pino 7 (McNeil 87); Larsen 5 (Nketiah 72, 7)

Subs not used: Benitez, Canvot, Chilwell, Doucoure, Hughes

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 9; Araujo 7 (Gomez 90), Jacquet 6, Van Dijk 6, Kerkez 6; Szoboszlai 7 (Nyoni 69, 7), Mac Allister 8; Gakpo 6 (Ngumoha 76) Wirtz 8, Barcola 7 (Munoz 69, 7); Isak 7 (Koumas 90)

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, McConnell, Tsimikas

Booked: Araujo, Barcola, Munoz, Mac Allister

Scorers: Mac Allister 40, Wirtz 54, Isak 89

Mac Allister resumed his bemusing role of the team's best aerial threat despite being their smallest player, Wirtz got a goal and assist, while Isak made it eight for the season to continue his prolific streak.

Bradley Barcola, meanwhile, proved what an asset he is despite a wasteful first half.

Those attackers were worthy of praise but no one deserved plaudits more so than goalkeeper, Alisson, who was player of the match in an illustration of Palace's first-half supremacy.

'I'm very pleased with Alisson's performance,' said Iraola. 'He has commanded the box very well and in games here a lot of things are normally happening in the boxes. He has shown the level he has for us. Overall we are getting good results away from home at difficult stadiums.'

The Brazilian is in the last year of his contract but put in his best performance for 18 months, dating back to a 1-0 win at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League knockouts. He will not go on international duty and instead rest up after an injury-hit few years.

He denied Adam Wharton with a glancing header, thwarted Daichi Kamada with a fierce shot and then tipped round Quenten Timber's effort from distance. Palace also rattled the bar through Yeremy Pino in a first half that really should have ended up differently.

Jorgen Strand Larsen also had the ball in the net but was offside.

As it was, though, Liverpool were the team to take their chance when it came after a period of dilly-dallying and playing the wrong ball, guilty again of indecisiveness similar to the flaws shown against Arsenal last weekend and in the 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce in midweek.

Liverpool led on 40 minutes when Alexis Mac Allister (centre left) scored from close range

The Argentine celebrates after breaking the deadlock for the Reds in the Premier League clash

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is facing the sack after his side dropped to the bottom of the Premier League.

Palace have won just two of their ten league matches this season, with Sunday's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool leaving them at the foot of the league for the first time in nearly nine years.

Sage is expected to lose his job during the international break, with Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank leading the race to replace the French coach.

However, Sage believes his side have been unlucky with results this season and has requested the hierarchy remain patient.

The 47-year-old, who left RC Lens for Palace in the summer to succeed Oliver Glasner, also admitted the Palace squad needs strengthening - perhaps to absolve himself of some blame.

'You can create the links between these two things,' Sage replied when asked whether being bottom of the league heading into the international break could see him sacked.

'But a lot of times I've said we deserved better and it was the case again on Sunday.

'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

'I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in that, and if it's not the case, they will take a decision.

'I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100% involved in what I have to do.

'We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be okay.'

Mac Allister was the scorer as he continued a fine resurgence this season, with Dominik Szoboszlai the supplier after a week where he too had been criticised. The Hungarian whipped a cross towards Mac Allister, which was glanced past Henderson for 1-0.

The former Brighton player ran straight towards the Palace fans behind the goal and taunted the supporters that were once his rivals on the south coast.

Liverpool weathered another storm at the start of the second half and soon found themselves two up. Barcola, who had left lots to be desired in the first half, swapped wings at the break and made his first attack count.

The Frenchman put the after-burners on and motored down the pitch before feeding Wirtz, who composed himself and passed into the net for 2-0. Iraola praised the run of Isak which took him away from the ball but dragged defenders with him to create space for his colleague.

Isak squandered a one-versus-one chance not long after but was not going to miss another one minutes later, when a blisteringly quick counter-attack was started by Trey Nyoni and ended with Wirtz feeding Isak, who skipped past Chris Richards and finished calmly.

The three goals will delight the hierarchy, with all three of the £100m boys – Isak, Barcola and Wirtz – registering at least one goal or assist apiece, one each in Wirtz's case.

Alexander Isak scored the visitors' third in the 89th-minute with this right-footed finish

Eddie Nketiah pulled one back for Palace from the penalty in second-half stoppage time

This victory would not have been possible, though, without Alisson, now 34 and in the final year of his deal. For all the attacking talent at Iraola's disposal, the Basque will be delighted at his team's defensive determination when under the kosh here as Palace had 10 first-half shots.

Iraola knows his team has flaws and they remain a work-in-progress. But despite a few challenging afternoons, they appear to be heading in the right direction.

The same cannot be said for Sage, whose side pulled one back in stoppage time through an Eddie Nketiah penalty after Milos Kerkez committed a careless foul.

Palace were unlucky in this game but the cold, hard truth is that the recent FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs feel a world away now as they enter the international break rock bottom of the Premier League.

West Ham also won a European trophy in the last five years and look where they ended up — that should set alarm bells ringing that no success lasts for ever and Palace are not too big for relegation.

Nketiah's goal felt like it was too little, too late and the sage advice for Palace supremo Steve Parish might be a reluctant change in the dugout.

#2125. Tomáš Souček Makes Blunt West Ham Promotion Admission

West Ham midfielder Tomáš Souček has admitted that the players must take their share of responsibility for the club’s disappointing Championship campaign, insisting that changing the manager doesn’t absolve them of blame.

Speaking to Czech publication Sport.cz, Souček acknowledged that results and performances haven’t been good enough and that West Ham must rediscover their winning mentality. He also made it clear that failing to return to the Premier League would represent failure.

It’s difficult to disagree with that sentiment, although I would argue that there wasn’t an awful lot wrong with the players’ attitudes during the 2-1 defeat against Blackburn Rovers. Mads Hermansen had something of a nightmare in goal, while Manor Solomon was ineffective when introduced from the bench. But I don’t think the overall performance was primarily a question of effort or attitude, which is why I’d argue that Scott Parker is the man who needs to fix things through better instruction and some new tactics.

As for Souček himself, there was a point during the Blackburn game when I thought we were crying out for his goalscoring ability. West Ham really only have two proven goalscorers in Jarrod Bowen and Tomáš Souček, and I felt the Czech midfielder should have been introduced much earlier.

Even in his brief appearance, Souček managed to get himself into a good goalscoring position, although his late header was saved. It was another reminder of something West Ham have been missing, particularly when the forwards have struggled to make an impact.

Souček is right that the players have a responsibility to improve, but from what I saw at Ewood Park, I don’t think a lack of effort was the biggest problem. Parker now has the international break to work on the team’s organisation and tactics, and that’s where I’d expect to see the most significant improvement.

#2124. Leeds vs Man Utd preview: Team news, form, injuries and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

Leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches. Their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah FK was the only comfortable win, but defeats to Manchester City and Atletico Madrid, alongside draws against Fulham and Tottenham, have raised questions about their form and Michael Carrick.

Leeds are waiting on Dan James, who returned from international duty with a back problem and missed the Arsenal game. Joe Rodon remains sidelined with a hamstring injury and is not expected back in full training until next month. Harry Wilson could return after being an unused substitute last weekend. Mateo Joseph is also among Leeds’ absentees.

Manchester United have their own concerns. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are doubts after picking up issues against Tottenham and missing Tuesday’s trip to Madrid. #2122. Independent Football Regulator approve West Ham board appointment

The Independent Football Regulator has approved James Taylor as West Ham’s new CFO, who can now join the West Ham board as company secretary and a director.

He replaces Andy Mollet, who retired in the summer after 14 years at West Ham.

IFR Outcome: The IFR determined that James Taylor is suitable for the role of Officer at West Ham United.

James Taylor (the applicant) submitted an application to the IFR for approval to carry out the role of SMF3: Chief Finance Function at West Ham United Football Club Limited (West Ham United).

Having assessed the application, under section 29 of the Football Governance Act 2026 (the Act), the IFR has determined that the applicant is suitable to be an officer, SMF3: Chief Finance Function, of West Ham United.

This means that, having considered the factors in section 37 of the Act and the IFR’s ODSE Rules, the IFR has concluded that the applicant:

Under section 82 of the Act, a person whom the IFR considers is directly affected by an IFR suitability determination may ask for it to be reviewed by a committee of the IFR Board who were not involved in making the original determination.

Any request must be made within 7 days of this determination’s publication date (or, if earlier, the date on which the IFR notified that person of this determination).

Further guidance on who the IFR may consider to be directly affected by its determinations, and how to request a review, can be found here.

After any requested review has been conducted, a concerned person, or other person with a sufficient interest, has a further right under section 84 of the Act to appeal the reviewer’s decision to the Competition Appeal Tribunal.

The IFR was formed in 2025 and includes former West Ham Executive Director Tara Warren as a non-executive director on its board.

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher said.

#2119. Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal set January transfer priorities as Fabrizio Romano delivers Piero Hincapié update

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal transfer news, Arsenal could approach the January transfer window with a different focus after Fabrizio Romano revealed that Mikel Arteta has no intention of weakening his defensive options.

Piero Hincapié has been linked with a move to Barcelona. There have been reports that a deal could be done involving Alejandro Balde, but Romano expects the Ecuadorian to stay at Emirates Stadium.

Arsenal have been strengthening their defensive department under Arteta. Hincapié only made the switch permanently from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer after joining on loan.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

However, Arsenal have little incentive to let him leave halfway through the season, as losing a two-in-one defender will cause problems for Arteta, given how much they need to do in multiple competitions.

Romano’s comments suggest that Arsenal are happy with their existing defensive unit and don’t want to cause any disruption to their balance. He also suggested that Hincapié is an important player for them, meaning he’s unlikely to leave in January.

That leaves Barcelona needing to explore alternative targets if they want to strengthen their backline. A deal involving Balde and Hincapié does not currently appear to be a realistic option.

The more interesting part of Romano’s report is Arsenal’s potential business at the other end of the field.

He feels they will be looking to make a move if the right attacking player comes up for grabs. But he doesn’t think they will make a signing just because they can in January.

This highlights the issues clubs face with mid-season transfers. Often selling clubs will be unwilling to lose key players, and finding suitable replacements can be tough.

As such, Arsenal are likely to look at the market to see what they can do. However, it looks like there could still be a forward brought in.

This is an important distinction. The point being made here is that whilst there is speculation around one particular player, Romano has indicated that Arsenal can strengthen their attacking options. This is not to say that any particular move is happening.

If Arteta keeps Hincapié, then Arsenal will maintain their defensive stability and possibly gain another option in attack.

Over the next few weeks we will get a better understanding of what is available to them. But for now it looks like Arsenal are not keen to lose Hincapié but will look to strengthen their attacking options if the right deal comes along.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

#2115. Scott Parker Must Restore West Ham’s Most Dangerous Weapon

One of the most disappointing aspects of West Ham’s performance against Blackburn Rovers at the weekend was the fact that Jarrod Bowen didn’t drift into the middle and cause havoc in the way he had against Cardiff City. Having watched what happened in Wales, I was genuinely excited about the possibilities for our captain under Scott Parker.

Because make no mistake about it, one of the biggest reasons the Hammers were able to overturn a three-goal deficit against Cardiff was the freedom afforded to Bowen. No longer was he restricted to the right wing, and suddenly he was popping up in central areas of the pitch, having a hand in all three West Ham goals.

As a result, I thought we might have discovered something rather special. Bowen could start on the right wing but effectively be given licence to operate as a number ten, providing West Ham with a completely different attacking threat. It was a whole new Jarrod Bowen, and he was incredibly effective at it.

That’s why I was so disappointed to see Bowen playing as a conventional, orthodox right winger against Blackburn. Having witnessed how dangerous he could be when drifting into central areas, I really thought Parker would look to exploit that again.

Instead, Bowen spent much of the match operating in his familiar position, and West Ham lost the unpredictability which had made him so effective against Cardiff. Of course, Blackburn were different opponents, but I couldn’t help feeling we’d missed a trick.

West Ham captain Bowen looked brilliant when seemingly given a free role against Cardiff City

The interesting thing is that I don’t believe Bowen needs to become an out-and-out striker to solve this problem. In fact, moving him permanently into the number nine position could simply deprive West Ham of their best creative player.

What excited me against Cardiff wasn’t the prospect of Bowen replacing the centre-forward. It was the possibility of him playing both roles at different moments, starting wide before moving inside and creating problems that opposition defenders struggled to deal with.

For all West Ham’s attacking problems, we already have a player capable of making things happen. Bowen demonstrated that against Cardiff, and I would argue that his movement and creativity were every bit as important as the goals themselves.

There’s no reason why he cannot continue to provide width when required while also moving into the space behind the striker. That flexibility could be particularly valuable with Joël Piroe leading the line, giving West Ham somebody to finish the opportunities Bowen creates.

I don’t want to see Parker abandon something which worked so spectacularly after just 45 minutes. We’ve spent much of this season struggling to create chances, yet against Cardiff we appeared to stumble upon a way of getting considerably more from our best player.

The international break gives Parker time to work on these attacking combinations, and I hope restoring Bowen’s freedom is near the top of his priorities. By the time West Ham face Preston North End, I’d like to see our captain operating with the same licence that made him almost unplayable in Cardiff.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

#2113. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

#2112. Arsenal 1-0 Hull City: Martin Ødegaard rescues Gunners with late winner at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal needed a moment of quality from their captain to overcome Hull City and claim a narrow 1-0 Premier League victory at the Emirates Stadium.

Martin Ødegaard scored in the 72nd minute as the hosts struggled to break down a resolute Hull side. It was much like I expected in my match preview, as Arsenal had to work hard to win this game.

The result gives them an extended lead at the top of the table. Ahead of Manchester City’s clash with Nottingham Forest. However, Mikel Arteta will be aware that his team did not play well in this game. It was far from a walk in the park.

Hull arrived at London looking to play an attacking game. Jakirovic’s side were well organised and looked to launch quick counter attacks.

They did have some positive moments in the first half, but Arsenal struggled to get into their attacking rhythm. Kai Havertz couldn’t capitalise on one good chance created by Ødegaard.

The hosts were hopeful of taking the lead after Havertz fell to the ground in the box after being pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

However, referee Farai Hallam’s initial decision was overturned after a VAR review showed Havertz was offside earlier in the attack, so Arsenal’s penalty was cancelled.

Another frustrating moment for the home side, who failed to score during the first half, despite dominating possession.

Arsenal came out strong after the break. However, Hull were still causing problems. Lewie Coyle was also walking a fine line after a yellow card in the first half and a late challenge on Christos Tzolis.

Arteta made a three-man change on the hour mark, bringing on Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino for Havertz and Declan Rice. Six minutes later he brought on Eberechi Eze and Piero Hincapié.

The breakthrough came from Madueke, forcing Konstantinos Tzolakis into action. The Hull keeper couldn’t hold his shot, and Ødegaard was quickest to react, scoring from the rebound.

The captain’s strike took the frustration out of Arsenal’s efforts and was a reward for their perseverance. It also provided another vital moment for the Norwegian. He’s had a tough campaign so far due to injuries.

Despite going behind, Hull never gave up in their search for an equaliser. However, Arsenal held on to their lead.

Arsenal dominated the game with 67% of possession and 21 shots, compared to just seven for Hull. Tzolakis put in a number of key interventions to keep the scoreline respectable.

Although they weren’t at their best, Arsenal were able to perform in the key moments of the game. Ødegaard’s goal meant that the Gunners earned three points and are sitting top of the Premier League heading into the international break.

#2111. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2110. Malo Gusto’s Kante Lesson Gives Chelsea A £75m Xabi Alonso Decision

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the important detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

The Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

Palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

Arsenal are still monitoring Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane as they weigh up options to strengthen their attack, according to BBC Sport.

The Gunners already know the 20-year-old well.

Kofane featured for Leverkusen when the sides met in last season’s Champions League round of 16, when Mikel Arteta’s team progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

The renewed interest follows heavy speculation during the summer.

In April, Kofane’s agent Eric Depolo said Arsenal’s interest was genuine and confirmed he was in contact with the club, claiming Kofane would give them a top striker for the next decade.

Kofane’s rise has been rapid. He moved from AS Nylon in Cameroon to Albacete in 2024, scoring eight goals in 20 Segunda Division games, before joining Leverkusen in July 2025.

He made 44 appearances in his first season in Germany, including 11 in the Champions League, and has three goals in six games this term. The frontman is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury.

#2108. Two days or two weeks – Michael Carrick future decision rolls into the international break

Manchester United will use the November international break to decide whether Michael Carrick stays on as head coach, after a three-game reprieve that delivered only one win.

According to The Guardian, Carrick came close to being sacked after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

Those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

Wilcox is now leading a review of Carrick’s position. He will consult Berrada before making a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who oversees the club’s sporting operations. Talks are expected to begin on Monday and continue through the break.

The league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

If he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

Carrick remains defiant. Speaking to Sky Sports News after the Villa draw, he admitted his side “haven’t won enough games” but insisted he expects to move forward.

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games, said Carrick after the late Villa draw.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”

If United do make a change, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reported to be Wilcox’s preferred candidate. Howe has been out of work since leaving St James’ Park during pre-season, after four and a half years in charge.

In the meantime, there are no plans to strengthen Carrick’s coaching staff.

For now, Carrick is expected to be in charge for United’s next match, against Liverpool. Whether three games were enough to convince the hierarchy should become clear before then.

The trip to Anfield could be do or die for the decorated former United midfielder.

He’s not likely to survive a heavy defeat at the home of the club’s fierce rivals, but a galvanising win would surely buy him time and goodwill.

That’s if he makes it through the next fortnight before then. A decision or indication could be two days or two weeks away.

The only certainty at Old Trafford is uncertainty.

#2107. William Saliba earns Arsenal U21s praise as defender continues comeback from injury

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

William Saliba Arsenal return: William Saliba has made a great impression during his return to action, according to Arsenal’s coaching staff. The U21s manager, David Horseman, praising his attitude and professionalism.

The 25-year-old played the first 45 minutes of Arsenal U21’s 5-2 win at Boreham Wood against Aston Villa on Sunday. Slowly making his way back from his three-and-a-half-month layoff.

Saliba was clearly a quality player, but it was his attitude which impressed Horseman. He worked well with the younger players and was a great example to follow throughout the morning.

The defender had been scheduled to play, and there were no new injury concerns behind his half-time withdrawal. He will return to the first team group as he continues to build up match fitness.

Saliba was praised by Horseman for his positive attitude since joining the club. His preparation, involvement in team meetings and ability to communicate with the younger players stood out.

He also showed his quality with the ball. His passing range helped the Arsenal attack and he made a good weighted pass that led to Marcell Washington running into space before Andre Harriman-Annous’ first goal.

Saliba didn’t see it as below his level to play in the game and really got into helping the academy players.

It set an example for the younger players in the squad. With an established first teamer keeping up the standards, there wasn’t much of an excuse for anyone else not to.

Saliba was not the only senior player to feature, with Marli Salmon as captain and Max Dowman also playing. Dowman, Maalik Hashi and Evan Mooney all scored, and Harriman-Annous added two goals.

It was another key step in Saliba’s return, as he featured in the matchday squad for Arsenal’s game against Slavia Prague after playing 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors friendly.

He wasn’t selected in the senior squad for their game against Hull City. With only nine subs allowed in the Premier League, Arsenal decided it was best to play him for the U21s.

The decision means that Saliba has been able to play competitive minutes to build up his fitness.

Arsenal will be hoping that he can now make a full recovery from his injury so that Mikel Arteta has another defensive option heading into a busy period for the club.

However, the U21s will have to maintain their high standards from the Aston Villa game without first team players such as Saliba, Salmon and Dowman.

We’ll keep you updated as and when we hear more information about the William Saliba Arsenal return.

#2106. Senegal Knockout Tie Gives Chelsea A Double Xabi Alonso Audit

Chelsea’s World Cup watch has moved beyond simple minutes management.

Senegal’s Round-of-32 meeting with Belgium now gives Xabi Alonso a live read on two very different development tracks.

Nicolas Jackson’s attacking authority is the immediate question. Mamadou Sarr’s defensive readiness is the longer-term one.

Chelsea confirmed that Senegal kept their knockout hopes alive with a 5-0 win over Iraq, with Jackson featuring from the bench.

Senegal have since moved into the knockouts, where they face Belgium in Seattle on Wednesday 1 July.

Jackson and Sarr travel into that game with contrasting club questions attached. Both still carry clear Chelsea relevance.

Sarr has not been the loudest Chelsea story of the tournament.

That may actually make this test more useful.

The 20-year-old is still moving through the awkward stage between prospect, squad option and saleable BlueCo asset.

Knockout football against Belgium can sharpen that picture quickly.

The timing is awkward in the best possible way for Chelsea. Alonso steps into a squad with expensive centre-backs, academy-trained options and a board still comfortable using the market aggressively.

A disciplined Sarr performance would not end that search. It would give the recruitment team a stronger internal benchmark before committing another major fee.

Chelsea need defenders who can hold a high line, cover wide channels and still pass through pressure. Belgium should ask those questions more directly than most group-stage opponents.

The context matters. Chelsea’s recall note recorded that Sarr returned from Strasbourg after 18 appearances across Ligue 1 and the Conference League.

The club also noted that he had already earned his first Senegal cap.

That is a different profile from an academy player being carried by reputation alone.

There is a statistical base behind the interest too. When Chelsea completed the deal, beIN SPORTS noted that Sarr made 27 Ligue 1 appearances in his first Strasbourg season.

He helped them keep 10 clean sheets. He also produced a team-high 20 blocks and made 25 interceptions.

Those numbers explain why this Belgium game is not just a sentimental World Cup subplot.

Alonso’s Chelsea defence is already crowded with Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Trevoh Chalobah and external targets still orbiting the plan.

ReadChelsea has already looked at why Colwill’s recovery story gives Alonso a defensive test. Sarr’s value is different.

He is still being evaluated as a physical, long-range defensive project.

Jackson’s role changes the editorial weight of the tie.

Chelsea’s striker picture has been messy for long enough. Any high-pressure international performance now carries wider meaning.

ReadChelsea has already framed the forward’s tournament as a live Senegal striker audit for Chelsea.

Belgium should stress both Chelsea questions at once.

Jackson has to offer penalty-box threat and transition security. Sarr, if trusted, has to defend space against a technically cleaner opponent.

He also has to show whether his recovery pace and frame translate under tournament pressure.

Sarr’s own mentality profile is worth noting. In a Chelsea World Cup Q&A, he named Lionel Messi, Sadio Mane and Paul Pogba as his tournament heroes.

His answer on Pogba focused on leadership and group mentality.

That lands neatly with the exact question Chelsea now need answered. Is there enough presence to go with the physical tools?

This is why Belgium feels like a pathway check rather than a routine World Cup watch item.

Chelsea do not need Sarr to solve the defence in July. They need clearer evidence on whether he belongs in Alonso’s first pre-season group.

He could need another loan. He could also become part of the club’s centre-back market arithmetic.

For Jackson, the question is more immediate. For Sarr, it is more structural.

Together, Senegal’s knockout tie gives Chelsea a rare clean look at two players on opposite ends of the same squad-building argument.

Who can help now, and who is worth protecting for later?

#2105. West Ham’s £20m Striker Has Two Weeks To Change Parker’s Mind

It would be fair to say that West Ham’s £20 million striker Pablo has been something of a victim of the club’s decision to sack Nuno Espírito Santo. As every Hammers fan knows, Nuno was a big fan of the Brazilian, who towards the end of his reign had moved to the top of the pecking order ahead of both Taty Castellanos and Joël Piroe.

Unfortunately for the former Gil Vicente forward, as soon as Scott Parker arrived, he dropped out of the squad altogether and didn’t appear to be anywhere near the first team. Pablo was absent from the matchday squads against both Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers, despite having been a regular selection under the previous manager.

There are two possible reasons for this, in my opinion. The first, and probably most obvious, is that Parker simply doesn’t deem him good enough to warrant a first-team squad place ahead of Piroe or Castellanos. The second could be the Championship’s squad eligibility requirements, with Soungoutou Magassa returning to the picture and potentially leaving Pablo as the overseas-trained player to miss out.

Now, I’m not going to sit here and pretend to be Pablo’s biggest fan. That would be disingenuous of me, because I’ve been critical of his finishing, overall technique and I still don’t believe he scores enough goals.

But let’s be fair, neither does Taty Castellanos, yet it always seems to be poor old Pablo who takes the brunt of the blame. Whatever his shortcomings in front of goal, nobody could reasonably question his work rate, which was clearly one of the reasons Nuno valued his pressing and willingness to chase lost causes.

The Brazilian could now be one of the unexpected beneficiaries of West Ham having so many players away on international duty. As things stand, Parker doesn’t have enough senior players available to put out a balanced eleven, even in a training match, which could provide Pablo with an opportunity to impress.

With Piroe representing Suriname and both of West Ham’s left-wing options, Manor Solomon and Edvin Austbø, also away with their countries, Parker has considerably fewer attacking players to work with than he would ordinarily expect.

Taty and Pablo will need to perform in training

It could therefore be that Pablo has a couple of weeks to impress his new boss, which in terms of effort and application I’ve little doubt he’ll do. The real question is whether Parker believes the striker possesses the necessary technique to operate within his preferred system.

After all, hard work should be a prerequisite rather than a reason for anybody to get into the team. And given Parker’s drive and intensity, I suspect everybody will be working hard once he has the opportunity to properly implement his methods.

But with West Ham’s pressing, or lack of it, also under the microscope, it could well be that Parker eventually chooses to select Pablo for exactly the same reasons Nuno Espírito Santo always did.

Pablo might not be the most technically gifted striker at the club, and his goalscoring record certainly leaves plenty to be desired. Nevertheless, if Parker wants somebody prepared to harass defenders, chase down possession and lead the press from the front, he already has a player who has demonstrated a willingness to do precisely that.

Whether that’s enough to earn him another chance remains to be seen, but the international break could provide an unexpected opportunity for a striker who appeared to have been completely forgotten.

#2104. Monaco summit adds unnecessary drama to Michael Carrick situation

Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington for Manchester United training as normal on Tuesday morning, while his bosses were preparing to decide his future in talks on the Mediterranean.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are flying to Monaco to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with the BBC reporting that the pair will recommend Carrick is sacked.The Guardian has indicated representatives of the Glazer family will also be involved.

The club insists the Monaco summit was pre-planned and is not solely about the head coach and while that may be true, it hardly matters.By allowing the meeting to become public knowledge, United have turned a straightforward football decision into unnecessary drama, compounding an already difficult situation.

What does is say about Man United in 2026 that a manager is given three games to secure his job, then left to train the squad during an international break while the executives are flying off to rule on his future? It’s farcical.

The latest chapter is another muddled process.Wilcox and Berrada met at Carrington the day after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October and agreed to give Carrick three more matches.A defeat at Chelsea, a win over Roma and a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa later, they appear to have reached the conclusion many expected a fortnight ago.

If the timeline holds, the decision will be made at Wednesday’s meeting, with an official announcement expected later in the week.United reportedly want to tell Carrick face to face, which means he could spend another day or two working under a cloud. In reality, it could be two days or two weeks.

The stakes could hardly be higher. United have won once in 10 league games, their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, and sit one point off the bottom in 18th place.

Should Carrick go, attention will turn quickly to his successor.ESPN reports that United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favoured candidate, while Eddie Howe has been named as Wilcox’s preferred choice. Antonio Conte has also been mentioned.

Carrick deserves better than this.Whatever the outcome, a club that wants to be taken seriously should not be settling its manager’s future in the full glare of the media while he is still out on the training pitch.

#2103. Atletico Madrid eye January move for Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Atletico Madrid are looking to make an ambitious January swoop for Martin Zubimendi after the Arsenal midfielder failed to convince Mikel Arteta to give him a regular starting spot.

The Spain international has started all seven of his Premier League appearances this season, coming off the bench. This has reportedly caught the eye of Diego Simeone, who wants to bolster his midfield in the winter window.

Atletico have marked Zubimendi as a possible target, according to Spanish radio station RNE via SPORT. Sporting director Mateu Alemany feels that there is still more to do with Simeone’s squad despite big investments in new players this summer.

If Zubimendi’s situation fails to improve at Arsenal, he could become one of the most wanted signings of January.

Zubimendi played a major role in Arsenal’s Premier League title-winning campaign last season. He made 34 league starts, scoring five goals and providing one assist.

He played a key role in the club’s run to the Champions League final. Since then Arsenal’s midfield has changed.

Injuries have hampered his campaign, but Myles Lewis-Skelly has returned to the midfield, and Bruno Guimaraes joined in the summer.

The 27-year-old has also expressed frustration at the lack of playing opportunities available to him. He was signed for £60 million from Real Sociedad to Arsenal just 18 months ago and has three-and-a-half years left on his contract.

Any move to Atletico would be a battle. Real Madrid are also reportedly fans of the midfielder, and he has also been linked with a move to Chelsea in recent months.

Atletico are keen to bring Zubimendi in alongside Pablo Barrios in central midfield.

It would be a dream combination for Simeone, and the Spanish club are willing to fund any move.

Another option could see him involved in a deal for Julian Alvarez. There are currently no talks about a potential swap deal.

Arteta has previously played down concerns about Zubimendi’s importance to Arsenal. Earlier this month, he highlighted the midfielder’s commitment and suggested injuries had affected his opportunities.

The Arsenal manager also made clear that Zubimendi would have chances to play, but would need to take them when they arrived.

That leaves the midfielder with an opportunity to work his way back into Arteta’s plans. However, Atletico’s reported interest could add another dimension to his situation as January approaches.

#2102. Michael Olise Gives Chelsea A Hard Xabi Alonso Wide-Player Benchmark

Michael Olise has moved from former Chelsea academy footnote to genuine Ballon d’Or conversation piece.

That should land at Cobham as more than a wistful what-if.

Bavarian Football Works relayed comments from former Chelsea and France winger Florent Malouda, who described the Bayern Munich forward as a live Ballon d’Or contender if France turn their World Cup run into silverware.

The point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

The market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

Chelsea’s official France preview noted that Malo Gusto was in the same squad as N’Golo Kante and former Blues academy player Olise. It was a neat reminder of how many Chelsea strands sit inside Didier Deschamps’ group.

Bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

That same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

That matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

Olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

This is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any new wide signing.

ReadChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

He is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

#2101. Winning is the only thing that matters to Rangers midfielder Dan Neil as Ibrox club continue to gain momentum in title challenge

Published: 13:52 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EST, 8 November 2026

Rangers midfielder Dan Neil admits he couldn’t care less about how his side go about picking up points as long as the wins keep coming.

The stand-in captain netted the crucial second in Saturday’s hard-fought victory over St Mirren in Paisley after Ryan Naderi had given the visitors a first-half lead from the penalty spot.

It was a result which extended Rangers’ unbeaten run to 12 in all competitions as they continue to build momentum following an unconvincing start to the campaign, and Neil insists that’s the only thing that matters at this stage.

He said: ‘I think every good team just finds a way to win.

‘Obviously, we’d like to win by four or five goals every single week but unfortunately that’s just not football. I do think it’s an area that we can improve on.

‘There’s been too many games this year where maybe we don’t get that second goal and it’s a bit nervy. Teams get a little bit of confidence off that and the momentum shifts.

Dan Neil savours the moment after putting the seal on Rangers' win with the second goal

‘I think it’s definitely something that we can improve on, putting teams to bed when we do go 1-0 up and go 1-0 up early doors when we’re creating chances.

‘But at the same time, finding a way to win is the most important way and whether that’s 1-0 or 5-0, at the end of the day it’s three points.’

While Rangers weren’t quite at their best in Paisley, they did more than enough to halt their poor recent run away from home.

Back-to-back 2-2 draws at Dundee and Hearts last month saw valuable points dropped in what is shaping up to be a tight title race, and Neil was delighted to get back to winning ways ahead of the international break.

‘The last two away results and performances really haven’t been us,’ said the former Sunderland man. ‘It was important that we didn’t have another one of them going into the break and have it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

‘Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. It’s important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you’ve seen that on Saturday night.

‘It was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us and make sure that we win the game. I think there was some good football played for the majority of the game and we also dug in when we had to. That’s credit to every single player in that dressing room.’
